points.summary: The campaign pledges to expand the repeat offender taskforce, deny bail to illegal immigrants arrested for violent felonies, establish a statewide prosecutor to support or replace local DAs, and allow impeachment of district attorneys who fail to prosecute violent criminals.
points.quote: illegal immigrants arrested for violent felonies must be denied bail and held behind bars while awaiting trail

points.summary: The campaign proposes cutting red tape in homebuilding by allowing third-party inspections, requiring 10-day occupancy determinations, pre-approving home designs across cities, allowing property additions by right, and withholding sales tax from cities that undermine housing reforms with luxury mandates.
points.quote: unnecessary regulations add thousands of dollars to the cost of a single-family home

points.summary: The campaign proposes capping monthly co-pays at $25 for life-saving medications like inhalers and epinephrine, and creating an Essential Benefits Health Insurance Plan to reduce premiums by nearly 20% for Texas families and small businesses.
points.quote: capping monthly co-pays at $25 for inhalers and epinephrine

points.summary: The campaign proposes opening municipal utility monopolies in cities like Austin and San Antonio to retail electric competition, allowing Texans to shop for cheaper electricity rates, and banning city utilities from charging unrelated fees or using profits as a slush fund.
points.quote: allow Texans to choose their electricity provider by opening city monopolies to retail electric competition

points.summary: The campaign proposes tuition discounts for summer courses ($500 for 1–5 credits, $1,000 for 6+) and requiring public universities to offer accelerated three-year, 90-credit-hour degree programs in high-demand fields so students graduate sooner and save on tuition and living expenses.
points.quote: Texas public universities will be required to offer accelerated 90 credit-hour degree programs in high-demand, high-paying fields

points.summary: The campaign proposes Student Success Academies for targeted reading and math support, limiting classroom screen time and 1-to-1 device use in favor of physical materials and direct instruction, dedicating 70% of education funding to classrooms, and increasing criminal penalties for teacher sexual abuse.
points.quote: Governor Abbott’s plan will limit the use of laptops, tablets, and other 1-to-1 devices in classrooms

points.summary: The campaign proposes allowing auto insurers to consider driving records so safe drivers save 10–30% on premiums, and establishing a $400 million roof fortification program providing up to $10,000 per homeowner to reduce home insurance costs from wind and hail damage.
points.quote: establishing a $400 million Texas roof fortification program

points.summary: Crowley will grow Wisconsin's economy through local ownership and union labor, expanding his Building Bridges Program statewide to revitalize commercial corridors and create good-paying jobs with strong labor standards.
points.quote: Crowley will grow an economy rooted in local ownership and union labor.

points.summary: Crowley will expand mobile health outreach, increase access to addiction treatment, and innovate EMS services across Wisconsin to ensure care reaches people where and when they need it.
points.quote: Crowley will expand mobile outreach, addiction treatment access, and EMS innovations across the state

points.summary: Crowley will build and preserve affordable housing in rural, urban, and suburban communities, cut barriers slowing new construction, and ensure homes are energy-efficient, resilient, and within reach for working families.
points.quote: Crowley will build and preserve affordable housing in rural, urban, and suburban communities across the state.

points.summary: Crowley will provide universal early childhood education, make new investments in public schools, and close the special education reimbursement gap to give every child a launchpad to success.
points.quote: Crowley’s plan includes universal early childhood education, new investments in public schools, and closing the special education reimbursement gap.

points.summary: Crowley will invest in solar power, energy retrofits, and clean infrastructure to create thousands of union jobs statewide, building on his record of cutting Milwaukee County emissions nearly 50%.
points.quote: Crowley will invest in solar power, energy retrofits, and clean infrastructure that creates thousands of union jobs across Wisconsin.

points.summary: Crowley will cap out-of-pocket childcare costs at 7% for all families, include paid family leave, and provide direct support for childcare providers to stabilize the sector.
points.quote: a 7% cap on out of pocket child care costs for all families

points.summary: Crowley will close Wisconsin's broadband gap, repair roads, and expand transit where needed, strengthening regional connections between rural communities and economic centers for seniors, workers, and families.
points.quote: Crowley will finally close Wisconsin’s broadband gap, repair roads, and expand transit where it’s needed

points.summary: Crowley will protect voting rights, push for nonpartisan redistricting at every level of government, and strengthen democratic systems to ensure every voice is heard.
points.quote: Crowley will protect voting rights, push for nonpartisan redistricting at every level, and strengthen the systems that ensure every voice is heard
